claims: Mortgage brokers act as an independent intermediary between borrowers and multiple lenders.
Mortgage brokers are usually paid a commission by the lender.
Lenders often pay mortgage brokers 1% to 2.75% of the loan amount as commission.
Lenders pay mortgage brokers a commission once the loan closes.
Borrowers sometimes pay mortgage brokers a fee directly.
Borrower-paid fees to mortgage brokers are paid either at closing or as a fee included in the loan amount.
Borrower-paid fees to mortgage brokers are typically paid upon closing.
Federal law prohibits broker compensation from varying based on the terms of the mortgage.
Mortgage brokers must register with the Nationwide Mortgage Licensing System and Registry (NMLS).
Mortgage brokers must meet specific state requirements.
Some lenders, notably big banks, do not work with brokers.
Mortgage brokers work with many lenders.
Loan officers work directly for one specific lender.
Loan officers work for a bank or credit union.
